data.title: Meet the data
data.explanation: Both models see the same 60,000 handwritten digits, not just one class. The official 10,000-image test set is kept out of generative training. Pixel intensities start in [0, 1]; the GAN training step maps them to [-1, 1] to match Tanh.
data.code:
def load_mnist(train=True):
    prefix = 'train' if train else 't10k'
    arrays = []
    for suffix, offset in [('images-idx3-ubyte.gz', 16), ('labels-idx1-ubyte.gz', 8)]:
        name = f'{prefix}-{suffix}'
        path = ROOT / 'datos' / name
        path.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        if not path.exists():
            temporary = path.with_suffix('.download')
            urlretrieve('https://storage.googleapis.com/cvdf-datasets/mnist/' + name, temporary)
            temporary.replace(path)
        with gzip.open(path, 'rb') as file:
            arrays.append(np.frombuffer(file.read(), np.uint8, offset=offset).copy())
    x = torch.from_numpy(arrays[0].reshape(-1, 1, 28, 28)).float() / 255
    return x, torch.from_numpy(arrays[1]).long()

vae_architecture.title: Compress, then reconstruct
vae_architecture.explanation: Two convolutions summarize local strokes. Separate heads predict a mean and log-variance for each of 64 latent coordinates. Reparameterization combines these learned quantities with Gaussian noise, allowing gradients to flow through sampling. The decoder expands a latent vector back into an image.
vae_architecture.formula: z = μ(x) + exp(½ log σ²(x)) ⊙ ε,  ε ~ N(0, I)
vae_architecture.code:
class VAE(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(1, 16, 4, 2, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(16, 32, 4, 2, 1), nn.ReLU(), nn.Flatten())
        self.mu = nn.Linear(32 * 7 * 7, LATENT)
        self.logvar = nn.Linear(32 * 7 * 7, LATENT)
        self.decoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(LATENT, 32 * 7 * 7), nn.ReLU(), nn.Unflatten(1, (32, 7, 7)),
            nn.ConvTranspose2d(32, 16, 4, 2, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.ConvTranspose2d(16, 1, 4, 2, 1), nn.Sigmoid())

    def forward(self, x):
        h = self.encoder(x)
        mu, logvar = self.mu(h), self.logvar(h)
        z = mu + (0.5 * logvar).exp() * torch.randn_like(mu)
        return self.decoder(z), mu, logvar

gan_architecture.title: Two networks, one game
gan_architecture.explanation: The generator turns 64 noise coordinates into an image using transposed convolutions. The discriminator reduces a real or generated image to one logit. Batch normalization and the DCGAN initialization make the optimization better behaved; they do not guarantee convergence.
gan_architecture.code:
def dcgan_weights(module):
    if isinstance(module, (nn.Conv2d, nn.ConvTranspose2d)):
        nn.init.normal_(module.weight, 0, 0.02)
    elif isinstance(module, nn.BatchNorm2d):
        nn.init.normal_(module.weight, 1, 0.02)
        nn.init.zeros_(module.bias)


def make_gan():
    generator = nn.Sequential(
        nn.Unflatten(1, (LATENT, 1, 1)),
        nn.ConvTranspose2d(LATENT, 32, 7, 1, 0, bias=False),
        nn.BatchNorm2d(32), nn.ReLU(True),
        nn.ConvTranspose2d(32, 16, 4, 2, 1, bias=False),
        nn.BatchNorm2d(16), nn.ReLU(True),
        nn.ConvTranspose2d(16, 1, 4, 2, 1, bias=False), nn.Tanh())
    discriminator = nn.Sequential(
        nn.Conv2d(1, 16, 4, 2, 1, bias=False), nn.LeakyReLU(0.2, True),
        nn.Conv2d(16, 32, 4, 2, 1, bias=False),
        nn.BatchNorm2d(32), nn.LeakyReLU(0.2, True),
        nn.Conv2d(32, 1, 7, 1, 0, bias=False), nn.Flatten())
    generator.apply(dcgan_weights)
    discriminator.apply(dcgan_weights)
    return generator, discriminator

vae_objective.title: Balance detail and structure
vae_objective.explanation: Reconstruction BCE measures how well the decoded image matches the input. KL divergence encourages the posterior to stay near a standard Gaussian, so randomly sampled latent vectors can be decoded. We sum pixels and latent dimensions, then average over the batch. The KL weight is one.
vae_objective.formula: L = BCE(x̂, x) + ½ Σ(μ² + σ² − 1 − log σ²)
vae_objective.code:
def vae_loss(reconstruction, real, mu, logvar):
    reconstruction_loss = F.binary_cross_entropy(reconstruction, real, reduction='sum') / len(real)
    kl = -0.5 * (1 + logvar - mu.square() - logvar.exp()).sum(1).mean()
    return reconstruction_loss + kl, reconstruction_loss, kl

gan_objective.title: Learn what looks real
gan_objective.explanation: The discriminator is penalized for assigning low probability to real images or high probability to fake images. Logits are passed directly into binary cross entropy for numerical stability. The generator uses the non-saturating objective shown in the training block: make fake images receive the real label.
gan_objective.formula: L_D = −E[log D(x)] − E[log(1 − D(G(z)))]; L_G = −E[log D(G(z))]

vae_training.title: Follow one update
vae_training.explanation: A batch passes through the encoder and stochastic latent variable into the decoder. Compute reconstruction and KL, clear old gradients, backpropagate, and update the model with Adam. This block repeats 469 times per epoch with batch size 128, including the final partial batch.
vae_training.code:
def vae_step(model, optimizer, real):
    reconstruction, mu, logvar = model(real)
    loss, bce, kl = vae_loss(reconstruction, real, mu, logvar)
    optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    return {'total': loss.item(), 'reconstruction': bce.item(), 'kl': kl.item()}

gan_training.title: Alternate the updates
gan_training.explanation: First update D using real images and detached generated images. detach prevents that update from changing G. Next freeze D’s parameters and backpropagate through its operations into G. D’s BatchNorm running statistics still update in training mode, as in the usual DCGAN loop.
gan_training.formula: update D with G fixed → update G through D
gan_training.code:
def gan_step(generator, discriminator, opt_g, opt_d, real):
    real = real * 2 - 1
    fake = generator(torch.randn(len(real), LATENT))
    real_logits, fake_logits = discriminator(real), discriminator(fake.detach())
    loss_d = gan_discriminator_loss(real_logits, fake_logits)
    opt_d.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
    loss_d.backward()
    opt_d.step()
    # Freeze D's parameters while differentiating through D into the generator.
    discriminator.requires_grad_(False)
    generated_logits = discriminator(fake)
    loss_g = F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(generated_logits, torch.ones_like(generated_logits))
    opt_g.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
    loss_g.backward()
    opt_g.step()
    discriminator.requires_grad_(True)
    return {'generator': loss_g.item(), 'discriminator': loss_d.item(),
            'd_real': real_logits.sigmoid().mean().item(),
            'd_fake': fake_logits.sigmoid().mean().item()}

sampling.title: Keep the experiment visible
sampling.explanation: Evaluation mode freezes BatchNorm statistics. A separate seeded generator creates the same 64 latent vectors for every snapshot, so changes reflect learning rather than new input noise. GAN outputs are mapped back to [0, 1]. Enlarged grids do not add resolution: each digit still has 28 × 28 pixels.
sampling.formula: fixed z → trained decoder / generator → recorded PNG

evaluation.title: Measure distributions, not promises
evaluation.explanation: A frozen MNIST classifier extracts 64-dimensional features. We L2-normalize them and compare real and generated distributions with an unbiased polynomial-kernel MMD estimator. It can be slightly negative from finite-sample noise. Predicted classes estimate coverage and entropy; a classifier can still be confidently wrong about malformed images.
